transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because things at work have gotten… hard to ignore. On this environmental modeling contract, I’m pretty sure people have been tracking my revisions and slipping errors into the datasets, making it look like I can’t lead the work.

My wife and some of the junior analysts say it’s probably just version-control mistakes, but… I don’t think that explains all of it.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, not voices like someone talking to me when nobody’s there. I haven’t really noticed that.
Have you been feeling unusually high, euphoric, or unusually irritable lately?
Not really high or euphoric, no. Irritable… maybe a bit, but I think anyone would be with what’s been going on. Nothing unusual, I guess.
Has anything happened that felt impossible by ordinary means, like someone controlling your thoughts or sending you messages in a way others couldn’t notice?

Not… controlling my thoughts, no. But messages, maybe not messages exactly. It’s more that on the contract, my revisions keep getting tracked too closely, and errors show up in the datasets after I’ve worked on them. It feels intentional. Like someone’s trying to make me look incapable of leading it.

Other people say it’s just version-control issues, but I don’t buy that.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day lately?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been worn down, but… depressed most of the day, every day? I wouldn’t say that.
Have you found yourself losing interest or motivation to do things you usually care about?

Some, yeah. I’ll sit at my desk for hours and not really start anything. Even the telescope in the garage… I used to go to astronomy nights, hikes, help the younger analysts. Lately I just don’t feel much pull to do any of it, or to talk to people.
Before all this started, had you had any major medical or neurological problem, like a head injury, seizure, stroke, or brain infection?
Not that I can think of. I mean… nothing like that comes to mind.
About how long have you been convinced that people at work are intentionally tracking your revisions and slipping errors into the datasets?
About two months, I guess. That’s when I became pretty sure it wasn’t just mistakes… that they were watching my revisions and putting things in there.
Have you had the feeling that your thoughts were being interfered with by someone else?

I don’t know about… my thoughts being interfered with exactly. It’s more that people on that environmental modeling contract are watching what I revise and then putting errors into the datasets so it looks like I can’t run the work. My wife says it’s just version-control stuff, but… I don’t think that explains it.
Have other people noticed that your facial expression or voice has become less expressive than usual?

Maybe. My wife has said I seem kind of flat lately… not talking much. I can sit for hours at my desk, or out in the garage with the telescope still covered, and just not really feel like starting anything. I used to do more—hiking, astronomy nights, helping the younger analysts—but lately I don’t have much pull toward any of it.
Since this started, have these beliefs about people at work sabotaging your datasets been present most days for at least a month?
Yes… most days. It’s been there for about two months now, that they’re tracking my revisions and putting errors in.
Have you started using any drugs or medications recently?
No… I don’t think so. Nothing new that I can think of.
Have other people commented that you seem less emotionally expressive than usual?

Yeah… my wife has said that. That I seem flat, I guess. I don’t talk much now. I’ll sit at my desk or in the garage with the telescope still covered, and I know I used to enjoy things, but… I don’t really feel much push to do them or talk to anyone.
Have other people told you that your speech has been hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?
I’m not sure. Nobody’s really said it like that to me. I don’t… I don’t notice myself jumping around, but I guess I wouldn’t always know.
Have people told you that your speech has become disorganized or hard to follow?
Not that I can recall. I mean… I don’t talk a lot lately, so maybe people don’t have much to go on. But no one’s said it’s disorganized, exactly.
Have you had the experience that your thoughts were being broadcast so that other people could know them without you speaking?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t had that, not like people can hear my thoughts or anything.
Lately, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day?
I don’t know… not most of the day, I don’t think. I’ve been kind of low sometimes, but it’s hard to say.
Have you heard voices talking about you when no one else was there?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed voices talking about me when nobody’s there.
Have you had any episodes of confusion or memory problems recently?
Not really… I mean, I forget small things sometimes, but nothing I’d call an episode. I haven’t noticed being confused like that.
Have you been speaking much less than usual lately?
Yeah… probably. I don’t really start conversations much. I can sit at my desk or out in the garage for hours and just not feel much reason to talk to anyone.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent persecutory delusion present most days for about 2 months, along with negative symptoms including affective flattening, reduced speech, social withdrawal, avolition, and reduced interest. There is no evidence of prominent mood episodes, substance/medication cause, or neurological/medical etiology. Delusional disorder is less likely because negative symptoms are present; acute polymorphic/acute schizophreniform psychosis is less supported because the picture is not polymorphic or rapidly changing; organic delusional disorder is not supported by history.
